title: Black Light FTL Safety Calibration Profile Registry

authority.purpose: Versioned numerical calibration packages for the FTL safety-certification runtime. These profiles translate established family distinctions into bounded runtime/gameplay coefficients without promoting the coefficients to setting canon.
sourceOrder: named race / vessel / manufacturer / installation source
Google Drive: The different lightspeed methods
authority.repairNote: The older ftl-calibration-registry.json still describes the design source path as unresolved. This registry binds the exact current Drive document ID/revision and must be preferred for safety-calibration provenance without rewriting the older mathematical registry wholesale.

scope.purpose: Neutral simulation baseline for comparing family-specific gravity, uncertainty, lookahead, and recovery behavior.
scope.runtimeUse: Permitted for generator simulation, encounter preparation, engineering exercises, and UI safety-state previews when no higher-authority named calibration exists.
scope.canonReach: None. Numerical values are game/simulation calibration only and must never be quoted as universal Black Light constants.

authority.coefficientPolicy: All values below are PROPOSED dimensionless runtime calibration. They preserve relative family behavior from authority but do not establish physical constants, historical capabilities, or named-race limits.

metric-compression.rationale: External curvature directly competes with engineered metric freedom; error sensitivity is substantial but continuous unwind can exist before commit boundaries.

gravitational-plane.rationale: Gravity is both roadway and hazard. Shear forks, hidden mass, and lane ambiguity justify the strongest baseline environmental and route-model sensitivity.

slipstream-shear.rationale: Gravity perturbs normal/Q correspondence and safe exits, while Q-boundary state remains a separate dominant hazard channel.

q-lattice.rationale: Direct gravity burden is lower than gravitic-plane operation, but reference, address, epoch, and covariance errors amplify strongly near distorted environments.

n-manifold.rationale: Ordinary-space gravity matters through embedding and return-map conditioning; projection uncertainty can dominate before raw field burden does.

fold-jump.rationale: Endpoint covariance and occupancy clearance make precommit uncertainty severe; postcommit correction must not be invented.

wormhole-gate.rationale: External tides and mouth synchronization impose substantial environmental burden, moderated by large fixed infrastructure and independent closure authority.

phase-displacement.rationale: Whole-object coverage, target authenticity, and reconciliation make model/reference error more dangerous than simple local gravity burden.

inertial-torch.rationale: Ordinary causal propulsion remains affected by gravity and navigation uncertainty but has no exotic field-collapse penalty.

scalingModel.policy: Scaling modifies burden, sensing geometry, synchronization, thermal rejection, structural reserve, and recovery authority separately. It must not be collapsed to power proportional to vessel mass.
equations: A_operational = min(M_sensor, M_recovery, M_structure, M_thermal, M_control)

namedOverrides.rule: Do not apply a family-specific coefficient override until the source-local gravitic-slipstream terminology is resolved to a consolidated operator family by evidence or higher authority.
Do not fabricate family coefficients for the Ar'nock derelict while its actual FTL family remains unresolved.

canonGuards: Profile numbers are not universal physical constants.
Profile numbers are not historical capability claims.
Named-source limits override this profile within their documented scope.
An unresolved named installation cannot inherit a family merely because a profile exists.
P0-P6 modifiers describe calibration behavior, not automatic historical progression dates.
Higher maturity increases safety margin and prediction authority but never guarantees perfect safety.
Gravity proximity remains hazardous across all exotic families; relative tolerance differs by operator.
Large-well emergence/commit restrictions remain authority-driven and cannot be removed by favorable tuning.
Protected recovery reserve cannot be spent to improve advertised nominal performance.
UI code cannot convert REJECTED or UNRESOLVED certification into selectable-safe state.
Scaling may worsen geometry, timing, heat, and observability even when power supply scales adequately.
Any named-race coefficient requires explicit source provenance or must remain DERIVED/PROPOSED.

selectionRules.conflictRule: Higher-authority narrower scope wins. Conflicting lower-authority numeric values are ignored and reported, not averaged.
selectionRules.missingRule: If required family or threshold data remain unresolved after authority resolution, return UNRESOLVED rather than inserting zero or the baseline value.
selectionRules.versionRule: Certificates must record profileId and profileVersion; replay uses the historical version unless explicitly recertified.
